dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kiṃcijjñair yā smṛtā śuddhiḥ sāśuddhiḥ śambhudarśane | na śucir hy aśucis tasmān nirvikalpaḥ sukhī bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 123: GRETIL and Pradīpaka read sā śuddhiḥ ('that is purity'); corrected to sāśuddhiḥ (sā aśuddhiḥ, 'that is impurity') with Wallis and The Mystery Within's Session Two (sa'suddhih); Singh's translation ('only impurity in the Śaiva system') supports it. Singh reports that Lakshmanjoo reads the second line na śucir nāśucis ('neither pure nor impure'), which Wallis's translation follows.
dharana.rendering: The purity that people of slight understanding uphold is impurity in Śiva's teaching; it is not purity but impurity. Therefore, free of thought-constructs, one becomes happy.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the purity criticised is outward physical purity (washing, bathing); the Trika system does not condemn it as such, only when it is taken as a passport to spiritual life at the cost of moral and spiritual purity, since it rests on thought-constructs centred on the body. Real purity is freedom from thought-constructs, and only that brings happiness. Singh reports Lakshmanjoo's reading na śucir nāśucis: 'it is neither purity nor impurity'; Wallis's translation follows it.
dharana.instruction: See your ideas of pure and impure as constructs of the mind, and set them down.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 98' = verse 123 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 123 = 'Purity and impurity (Y98 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 123 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 123 'Dharana 100', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 98. Not followed.

source_disagreements: Verse 123: GRETIL and Pradīpaka read sā śuddhiḥ ('that is purity'), as does The Mystery Within's parallel section (sa suddhih); Wallis and the Session Two list read sāśuddhiḥ ('that is impurity'), which Singh's translation supports. Lakshmanjoo (via Singh) reads na śucir nāśucis ('neither pure nor impure'), followed by Wallis's translation.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 123 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a line drawn between 'pure' and 'impure', seen to be only a line in the mind, and set down.
geometry.svg_hint: a dividing line across a field, drawn faint, fading away
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Set down the line
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the mental line between pure and impure is seen as a construct and set down. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Ideas of pure and impure, seen as thought-constructs
attention.secondary: The ease of not dividing experience that way

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: The purity that people of slight understanding uphold is impurity in Śiva's teaching; it is not purity but impurity. Therefore, free of thought-constructs, one becomes happy.
adiyogi.method_summary: Notice where you divide experience into pure and impure, clean and unclean, worthy and unworthy. See those divisions as constructs of the mind. Set them down, and rest in the ease that follows.

honesty.disclosure: Door 098 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 98 (verse 123) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 098 is dharana 98, verse 123. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is about inner judgement, not hygiene: ordinary washing, care of the body and food safety still apply. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
